stimuli.text: Researchers investigated whether cognitive-behavioral therapy reduces depression. They recruited 90 adults diagnosed with major depressive disorder and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition received twelve weekly sessions of cognitive-behavioral therapy. Participants in the other condition were placed on a waiting list for twelve weeks and were treated afterward. The researchers then recorded each participant's score on a standard depression questionnaire after twelve weeks.

Researchers investigated whether the wording of a question changes what witnesses remember. They recruited 100 adult volunteers who watched a film of a car accident and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition were asked how fast the cars were going when they smashed into each other. Participants in the other condition were asked how fast the cars were going when they contacted each other. The researchers then recorded the speed in kilometers per hour that each participant wrote down. The results are shown in the table. The difference between the two groups had a p value of 0.01.

rows.group: The group asked the question with the word 'smashed'
The group asked the question with the word 'contacted'

stimuli.text: Researchers collected data from 1,200 teenagers. For each one, they recorded the number of hours of social media use per day and score on a depression questionnaire. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.28.

Researchers investigated whether an expected reward reduces children's later interest in drawing. They recruited 60 preschool children who enjoyed drawing and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition were promised a certificate for drawing and received it. Children in the other condition drew with no reward mentioned. The researchers then recorded the number of minutes that each child chose to spend drawing during free time one week later.

Researchers collected data from 300 families. For each one, they recorded the warmth of parenting, as rated by observers and the child's self-esteem score. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.48.

Researchers investigated whether the color of a drink affects the ability to identify its flavor. They recruited 70 adult volunteers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition tasted ten fruit drinks whose colors did not match their flavors. Participants in the other condition tasted the same ten drinks with matching colors. The researchers then recorded the number of flavors out of ten that each participant named correctly.

Researchers investigated whether a phone conversation reduces what drivers notice. They recruited 64 licensed drivers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition held a hands-free phone conversation while using a driving simulator. Participants in the other condition used the driving simulator without a phone. The researchers then recorded the number of road signs out of 30 that each participant failed to notice.
Researchers collected data from 300 fifth-grade students. For each one, they recorded working memory span and reading comprehension score. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.52.

Researchers investigated whether spreading study sessions out improves long-term retention. They recruited 90 high school students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition studied a list of 40 words in six ten-minute sessions on six different days. Participants in the other condition studied the same list in a single sixty-minute session. The researchers then recorded the number of words out of 40 that each participant recalled on a test one month later.

Researchers investigated whether nausea after a new taste produces an aversion to that taste. They recruited 40 laboratory rats and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Rats in one condition drank sweetened water and were then given an injection that causes mild nausea. Rats in the other condition drank sweetened water and were then given a harmless salt-water injection. The researchers then recorded the volume in milliliters of sweetened water that each rat drank the next day.

Researchers investigated whether keeping a gratitude journal raises well-being. They recruited 110 adult volunteers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition wrote down three things they were grateful for every night for a month. Participants in the other condition wrote down three things they had done every night for a month. The researchers then recorded each participant's rating of life satisfaction on a scale from 1 to 10 at the end of the month. The results are shown in the table. The difference between the two groups had a p value of 0.41.

rows.group: The group that wrote about gratitude
The group that wrote about daily events

stimuli.text: Researchers investigated whether the presence of other people slows the reporting of an emergency. They recruited 80 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition were filling in a form in a room with four other people when smoke began to enter the room. Participants in the other condition were filling in the form alone when smoke began to enter the room. The researchers then recorded the time in seconds before each participant left the room to report the smoke.

Researchers investigated whether a night without sleep slows reaction time. They recruited 60 adult volunteers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition stayed awake all night in the laboratory. Participants in the other condition slept for eight hours in the laboratory. The researchers then recorded the average time in milliseconds that each participant took to press a button when a light appeared.

Researchers investigated whether a smiling expression makes cartoons seem funnier. They recruited 90 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition held a pen between their teeth, which produces a smile. Participants in the other condition held a pen between their lips, which prevents a smile. The researchers then recorded the rating from 1 to 10 that each participant gave to a set of cartoons.
Researchers collected data from 450 adults. For each one, they recorded optimism score and the number of days of illness in a year. The correlation between the two measures was r = −0.30.

Researchers investigated whether regular aerobic exercise improves memory in older adults. They recruited 100 adults aged 60 to 75 and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition walked briskly for 40 minutes three times a week for six months. Participants in the other condition did gentle stretching for the same amount of time. The researchers then recorded the number of locations that each participant correctly recalled on a spatial memory test. The results are shown in the table. The difference between the two groups had a p value of 0.41.

rows.group: The group that did gentle stretching

stimuli.text: Researchers investigated whether children imitate aggressive behavior that they observe. They recruited 72 preschool children and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition watched a video of an adult hitting an inflatable doll. Children in the other condition watched a video of an adult playing quietly with other toys. The researchers then recorded the number of times that each child hit the doll during ten minutes of free play.

Read the summary of a hypothetical study, then answer parts A to F.

**Introduction.** Researchers investigated whether mindfulness meditation lowers stress. They hypothesized that the daily activity would affect stress.

**Participants.** The sample was 84 office workers, recruited from one city. All participants gave informed consent, were told they could withdraw at any time, and were debriefed afterward. The plan was approved by an institutional review board.

**Method.** The participants were randomly assigned to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition practiced mindfulness meditation for twenty minutes a day for eight weeks. Participants in the other condition listened to an audiobook for twenty minutes a day for eight weeks. The researchers recorded the level of the stress hormone cortisol in a saliva sample from each participant.

**Results.** The group that meditated: mean cortisol level (nmol/l) = 9.8. The group that listened to an audiobook: mean cortisol level (nmol/l) = 13.5. The difference was statistically significant (p = 0.01).

Use the three hypothetical sources to answer the question: **Do rewards increase motivation?**

**Source A.** In an experiment, 60 preschool children who liked drawing were randomly assigned to draw for a promised certificate or to draw with no reward. A week later, during free play, the rewarded children chose to draw for a mean of 6.5 minutes and the unrewarded children for 13.8 minutes (p = 0.01).

**Source B.** In a study of 200 call-center workers, half were randomly assigned to receive a bonus for each sale. Over a month, the bonus group made a mean of 41 sales and the comparison group a mean of 33 (p = 0.02). When the bonus ended, the bonus group's sales fell to a mean of 30.

**Source C.** A survey of 500 university students found that students who said they studied mainly because they found their subject interesting had higher grades and reported less burnout than students who said they studied mainly for grades or money (r = +0.40 between interest and grades).

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the understanding that quantity stays the same when shape or arrangement changes?

options.why: Animism is the belief of young children that lifeless objects have feelings and intentions.
Correct. Conservation is the understanding that quantity stays the same when shape or arrangement changes.
Reversibility is the understanding that an action can be undone to return things to their original state.
Object permanence is the understanding that things continue to exist when they are out of sight.

questions.explanation: Conservation is the understanding that quantity stays the same when shape or arrangement changes.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the judging of how likely something is by how easily examples come to mind?

options.why: Correct. The availability heuristic is the judging of how likely something is by how easily examples come to mind.
Framing is the way the wording of an issue affects decisions and judgments.
Priming is the activation, often without awareness, of certain associations that then influence perception or behavior.
The representativeness heuristic is the judging of how likely something is by how well it matches a prototype, while ignoring base rates.

questions.explanation: The availability heuristic is the judging of how likely something is by how easily examples come to mind.

questions.stem: Which group served as the control group?

options.text: The group on the waiting list
options.why: Correct. The control group is the comparison group that does not receive the treatment being tested.
Only the comparison group is the control group.
This group received the treatment being tested: it is the experimental group.

options.text: Neither group, because the study had no comparison condition
options.why: The second condition is the comparison.

questions.explanation: The control group is the comparison group that does not receive the treatment being tested.

questions.stem: A door swinging open casts a changing image on the retina, yet it still looks rectangular. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Size constancy is the perception that an object keeps the same size even when its image on the retina changes.
Color constancy is the perception that an object keeps the same color under different lighting.
Apparent movement is the perception of motion when a series of still images or lights is shown in quick succession.
Correct. Shape constancy is the perception that an object keeps the same shape even when the viewing angle changes.

questions.explanation: Shape constancy is the perception that an object keeps the same shape even when the viewing angle changes.

questions.stem: Which statement about the results is best supported?

options.text: The difference between the groups is statistically significant, so it is unlikely to be due to chance
options.why: Correct. A p value below 0.05 means a difference this large would rarely occur by chance alone.

options.text: The two groups had the same average result
options.why: The table shows different averages.

options.text: The results prove that every individual in the first group differed from every individual in the second
options.why: The table reports group averages, not individual scores.

options.text: The difference between the groups is probably due to chance
options.why: A p value of 0.01 is below 0.05, so chance is an unlikely explanation.

questions.explanation: A p value below 0.05 means a difference this large would rarely occur by chance alone.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as Erikson's stage in young adulthood, in which people seek close, lasting relationships?

options.why: Identity versus role confusion is Erikson's stage in adolescence, in which teenagers work out who they are.
Integrity versus despair is Erikson's stage in late adulthood, in which people look back on life with satisfaction or regret.
Correct. Intimacy versus isolation is Erikson's stage in young adulthood, in which people seek close, lasting relationships.
Generativity versus stagnation is Erikson's stage in middle adulthood, in which people seek to contribute to the world through family and work.

questions.explanation: Intimacy versus isolation is Erikson's stage in young adulthood, in which people seek close, lasting relationships.

questions.stem: After hearing a list of fifteen words, people recall the first few and the last few best. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: The primacy effect is the tendency to remember the first items in a list well.
The recency effect is the tendency to remember the last items in a list well.
The spacing effect is the finding that study spread over time produces better long-term memory than study crammed together.
Correct. The serial position effect is the tendency to remember the first and last items in a list better than the middle ones.

questions.explanation: The serial position effect is the tendency to remember the first and last items in a list better than the middle ones.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the view that a disorder develops when an inherited vulnerability is triggered by stressful experience?

options.why: The biopsychosocial model is the view that disorders result from the interaction of biological, psychological and social factors.
Comorbidity is the presence of two or more disorders in the same person at the same time.
Correct. The diathesis-stress model is the view that a disorder develops when an inherited vulnerability is triggered by stressful experience.
An eclectic approach is the use of techniques from several types of therapy, depending on the client's problem.

questions.explanation: The diathesis-stress model is the view that a disorder develops when an inherited vulnerability is triggered by stressful experience.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the temporary support that a more skilled person gives a learner and gradually removes?

options.why: The zone of proximal development is the gap between what a learner can do alone and what the learner can do with help.
Crystallized intelligence is the accumulated knowledge and verbal skills that tend to increase with age.
Correct. Scaffolding is the temporary support that a more skilled person gives a learner and gradually removes.
Fluid intelligence is the ability to reason quickly and abstractly, which tends to decline in older adulthood.

questions.explanation: Scaffolding is the temporary support that a more skilled person gives a learner and gradually removes.

questions.stem: If the data were shown on a scatterplot, what pattern would the points form?

options.text: A shapeless cloud with no slope
options.why: That would show a correlation near zero.

options.text: A loose band that slopes downward from left to right
options.why: That would show a negative correlation.

options.text: A loose band that slopes upward from left to right
options.why: Correct. A moderate positive correlation appears as a band of points sloping upward.
Only a correlation of +1.00 or −1.00 gives a perfect line.

questions.explanation: A moderate positive correlation appears as a band of points sloping upward.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a schema?

options.text: The changing of an existing schema to fit new information
options.why: That describes accommodation.

options.text: A mental grouping of similar objects, events, ideas or people
options.why: That describes a concept.

options.text: The interpretation of a new experience in terms of an existing schema
options.why: That describes assimilation.

options.text: A mental framework that organizes and interprets information
options.why: Correct. This is what a schema means.

questions.explanation: A schema is a mental framework that organizes and interprets information.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the operational definition of the dependent variable?

options.text: The number of minutes that each child chose to spend drawing during free time one week later
options.why: Correct. An operational definition states exactly how a variable is measured.
This is the independent variable.

options.text: The random assignment of each one to a condition
options.why: This is a control procedure, not a definition of a variable.
This names the variable but does not say how it was measured.

questions.explanation: An operational definition states exactly how a variable is measured.

questions.stem: A man is certain that government agents have planted a transmitter in his tooth, and no evidence can change his mind. Which symptom is this?

options.why: Flat affect is a lack of emotional expression in the face and voice.
Correct. A delusion is a false belief, often of persecution or grandeur, that a person holds despite clear evidence against it.
A hallucination is a sensory experience, such as hearing voices, that occurs without any outside stimulus.
Disorganized speech is the jumbled, illogical speech, sometimes called word salad, that is a symptom of schizophrenia.

questions.explanation: A delusion is a false belief, often of persecution or grandeur, that a person holds despite clear evidence against it.

questions.stem: A therapist refuses to exaggerate her qualifications or to make false claims about how well a treatment works. Which ethical principle is she following?

options.why: Nonmaleficence is the ethical principle that psychologists must avoid doing harm.

options.text: Respect for people's rights and dignity
options.why: Respect for people's rights and dignity is the ethical principle that psychologists must protect privacy, confidentiality and the right of people to make their own choices.
Fidelity is the ethical principle that psychologists must be trustworthy and keep their professional promises.
Correct. Integrity is the ethical principle that psychologists must be honest and accurate.

questions.explanation: Integrity is the ethical principle that psychologists must be honest and accurate.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes withdrawal?

options.text: A drug that increases the action of a neurotransmitter, for example by mimicking it
options.why: That describes an agonist.

options.text: The need for larger doses of a drug to get the same effect after repeated use
options.why: That describes tolerance.

options.text: The unpleasant physical and psychological symptoms that follow stopping an addictive drug
options.why: Correct. This is what withdrawal means.

options.text: A drug that keeps a neurotransmitter in the synapse longer by blocking its reabsorption
options.why: That describes a reuptake inhibitor.

questions.explanation: Withdrawal is the unpleasant physical and psychological symptoms that follow stopping an addictive drug.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes restoration?

options.text: The repair of body and brain tissue that takes place during sleep
options.why: Correct. This is what restoration means.

options.text: The theory that dreaming helps sort and strengthen the day's memories
options.why: That describes the consolidation theory.

options.text: The theory that dreams are the brain's attempt to make sense of random neural activity during sleep
options.why: That describes the activation-synthesis theory.

options.text: The strengthening of memories that takes place during sleep
options.why: That describes memory consolidation.

questions.explanation: Restoration is the repair of body and brain tissue that takes place during sleep.

questions.stem: A theory says that people thrive when they feel capable, feel in control of their choices and feel connected to others. Which theory is this?

options.why: Instinct theory is the theory that behavior is driven by fixed, inborn patterns that are not learned.
The Yerkes-Dodson law is the principle that performance is best at a moderate level of arousal.
Correct. Self-determination theory is the theory that people are motivated by needs for competence, autonomy and relatedness, either from within or from outside.
Arousal theory is the theory that people are motivated to keep an ideal level of alertness and stimulation.

questions.explanation: Self-determination theory is the theory that people are motivated by needs for competence, autonomy and relatedness, either from within or from outside.

questions.stem: After many years on antipsychotic medication, a patient develops uncontrollable movements of the mouth and tongue. Which side effect is this?

options.why: An antipsychotic drug is a drug that reduces hallucinations and delusions by blocking dopamine receptors.
Correct. Tardive dyskinesia is the involuntary movements of the face and tongue that can result from long-term use of antipsychotic drugs.
Lithium is the mood-stabilizing drug used to treat bipolar disorder.
An antidepressant is a drug, such as an SSRI, that treats depression and anxiety by raising the availability of serotonin or norepinephrine.

questions.explanation: Tardive dyskinesia is the involuntary movements of the face and tongue that can result from long-term use of antipsychotic drugs.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes unconditional positive regard?

options.text: The attitude of total acceptance toward another person, whatever they say or do
options.why: Correct. This is what unconditional positive regard means.

options.text: In psychodynamic theory, the store of thoughts, wishes and memories that a person is not aware of but that still influences behavior
options.why: That describes the unconscious.

options.text: In psychodynamic theory, a method the ego uses without awareness to reduce anxiety by distorting reality
options.why: That describes a defense mechanism.

options.text: A personality test, such as an inkblot test, that asks people to interpret unclear images in order to reveal hidden feelings
options.why: That describes a projective test.

questions.explanation: Unconditional positive regard is the attitude of total acceptance toward another person, whatever they say or do.

questions.stem: At two months, a baby makes soft 'ooh' and 'aah' sounds. Which stage of language development is this?

options.why: Overgeneralization is the applying of a grammar rule too widely, as in 'goed' or 'mouses'.
Babbling is the stage from about four months in which infants produce many consonant-vowel sounds, such as 'ba-ba'.
The one-word stage is the stage from about age 1 in which a child speaks mostly in single words.
Correct. Cooing is the vowel-like sounds, such as 'ooh', that infants make from about two months.

questions.explanation: Cooing is the vowel-like sounds, such as 'ooh', that infants make from about two months.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a possible third variable that could explain the correlation?

options.text: The warmth of parenting, as rated by observers
options.why: This is one of the two variables that were measured.
This is one of the two variables that were measured.
This is the statistic, not a variable.

options.text: The level of financial stress in the family
options.why: Correct. A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.

questions.explanation: A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.

questions.stem: A person notices when 1 kg is added to a 10 kg load but needs 5 kg to be added before noticing a change in a 50 kg load. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: The absolute threshold is the weakest level of a stimulus that a person can detect half of the time.
Transduction is the conversion of physical energy, such as light or sound, into neural impulses.
Correct. Weber's law is the principle that two stimuli must differ by a constant proportion, not a constant amount, to be noticed.
Sensory interaction is the way one sense influences another, as when smell affects taste.

questions.explanation: Weber's law is the principle that two stimuli must differ by a constant proportion, not a constant amount, to be noticed.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the parenting style that sets firm rules but explains them, listens and is warm?

options.why: Permissive parenting is the parenting style that makes few demands and sets few limits.
Temperament is a person's characteristic emotional reactivity and intensity, which appears early in life.
Authoritarian parenting is the parenting style that sets strict rules and expects obedience, with little warmth or discussion.
Correct. Authoritative parenting is the parenting style that sets firm rules but explains them, listens and is warm.

questions.explanation: Authoritative parenting is the parenting style that sets firm rules but explains them, listens and is warm.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a scatterplot?

options.text: A relationship in which two variables rise and fall together
options.why: That describes a positive correlation.

options.text: The possibility that an unmeasured factor causes the relationship between two correlated variables
options.why: That describes the third variable problem.

options.text: The number from −1.00 to +1.00 that shows the direction and strength of a relationship
options.why: That describes the correlation coefficient.

options.text: A graph in which each point shows one individual's values on two variables
options.why: Correct. This is what a scatterplot means.

questions.explanation: A scatterplot is a graph in which each point shows one individual's values on two variables.

questions.stem: After staring at a green square and then looking at a white wall, Eli sees a red square. Which theory best explains this afterimage?

options.why: Prosopagnosia is the inability to recognize faces, even familiar ones, after brain damage.
Monochromatism is a rare form of color blindness in which a person sees only shades of gray.
Correct. The opponent-process theory is the theory that color is processed in opposing pairs: red–green, blue–yellow and black–white.
Dichromatism is a form of color vision deficiency in which one of the three types of cones does not work.

questions.explanation: The opponent-process theory is the theory that color is processed in opposing pairs: red–green, blue–yellow and black–white.

questions.stem: A dog already salivates to a tone. A light is then repeatedly shown just before the tone, and the dog begins to salivate to the light. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Extinction is the weakening of a conditioned response when the conditioned stimulus is repeatedly presented alone.
Acquisition is in classical conditioning, the first stage, in which the neutral stimulus is paired with the unconditioned stimulus and the response is learned.
Stimulus discrimination is the learned ability to respond to the conditioned stimulus but not to similar stimuli.
Correct. Higher-order conditioning is the pairing of a new neutral stimulus with an existing conditioned stimulus to create a second conditioned stimulus.

questions.explanation: Higher-order conditioning is the pairing of a new neutral stimulus with an existing conditioned stimulus to create a second conditioned stimulus.

questions.stem: The highest score on a test is 98 and the lowest is 41, giving a value of 57. Which statistic is this?

options.why: Correct. The range is the difference between the highest and lowest scores.
The mode is the score that occurs most often.
The mean is the arithmetic average of a set of scores.
The standard deviation is the measure of how much scores vary around the mean.

questions.explanation: The range is the difference between the highest and lowest scores.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a test that measures what a person has already learned?

options.why: Stereotype threat is the worry about confirming a negative stereotype about one's group, which can lower performance.
Stereotype lift is the boost in performance that comes from awareness that another group is negatively stereotyped.
An aptitude test is a test that predicts a person's ability to learn or perform in the future.
Correct. An achievement test is a test that measures what a person has already learned.

questions.explanation: An achievement test is a test that measures what a person has already learned.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the influence of a researcher's expectations on the results of a study?

options.why: Self-report bias is the inaccuracy that arises when people describe their own behavior or feelings.
Hindsight bias is the tendency, after learning an outcome, to believe one would have predicted it.
Correct. Experimenter bias is the influence of a researcher's expectations on the results of a study.
Overconfidence is the tendency to be more certain than correct about one's own judgments.

questions.explanation: Experimenter bias is the influence of a researcher's expectations on the results of a study.

questions.stem: People asked to hold a pen between their teeth, which forces a smile, rate cartoons as funnier. This finding supports which of the following?

options.why: Correct. The facial-feedback hypothesis is the idea that the expression on a person's face can influence the emotion the person feels.
The broaden-and-build theory is the theory that positive emotions widen a person's awareness and help build lasting skills and resources.
Cognitive appraisal is the interpretation of a situation, which shapes the emotion a person feels.
Universal emotions is the basic emotions, such as happiness, sadness, fear and anger, whose facial expressions are recognized across cultures.

questions.explanation: The facial-feedback hypothesis is the idea that the expression on a person's face can influence the emotion the person feels.

questions.stem: Aaron spends his weekends skydiving and rock climbing. Which form of sensation seeking is this?

options.why: Boredom susceptibility is the form of sensation seeking that involves a strong dislike of repetition and routine.
Disinhibition is the form of sensation seeking that involves a loss of self-restraint, as at wild parties.
Experience seeking is the form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for new experiences through travel, art and unusual lifestyles.
Correct. Thrill and adventure seeking is the form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for risky physical activities.

questions.explanation: Thrill and adventure seeking is the form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for risky physical activities.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes an implicit attitude?

options.text: An attitude that a person holds without being aware of it
options.why: Correct. This is what an implicit attitude means.

options.text: Unjustified negative behavior toward a group and its members
options.why: That describes discrimination.

options.text: A generalized belief about a group of people
options.why: That describes a stereotype.

options.text: The tendency to judge other cultures by the standards of one's own culture
options.why: That describes ethnocentrism.

questions.explanation: An implicit attitude is an attitude that a person holds without being aware of it.

questions.stem: Although Nell has handled coins thousands of times, she cannot say which way the head faces, because she never paid attention to it. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: The forgetting curve is the pattern in which memory fades quickly at first and then levels off.
The tip-of-the-tongue phenomenon is the temporary inability to retrieve a word that one is sure one knows.
Repression is in psychodynamic theory, the pushing of anxiety-arousing memories out of awareness.
Correct. Encoding failure is forgetting that happens because the information never entered long-term memory.

questions.explanation: Encoding failure is forgetting that happens because the information never entered long-term memory.

questions.stem: Sam is warm, quick to forgive and always willing to help. He would score high on which Big Five trait?

options.why: Openness to experience is the Big Five trait of being imaginative, curious and willing to try new things.
Extraversion is the Big Five trait of being sociable, outgoing and energetic.
Correct. Agreeableness is the Big Five trait of being kind, trusting and cooperative.
Emotional stability is the Big Five trait of being calm and secure rather than anxious and moody.

questions.explanation: Agreeableness is the Big Five trait of being kind, trusting and cooperative.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the reducing of stress by changing the stressor itself or the way one deals with it?

options.why: Correct. Problem-focused coping is the reducing of stress by changing the stressor itself or the way one deals with it.
Emotion-focused coping is the reducing of stress by managing one's emotional reaction rather than the stressor.
Immune suppression is the weakening of the body's defenses against illness during long-term stress.
Hypertension is persistently high blood pressure, which is made more likely by chronic stress.

questions.explanation: Problem-focused coping is the reducing of stress by changing the stressor itself or the way one deals with it.

questions.stem: When a classmate arrives late, Ian decides, 'She is a lazy and disorganized person.' Which kind of explanation is this?

options.why: Downward social comparison is the comparing of oneself with people who are doing worse.
A situational attribution is an explanation of behavior that points to outside circumstances.
An external locus of control is the belief that outcomes are decided by luck, fate or other people.
Correct. A dispositional attribution is an explanation of behavior that points to the person's own traits or character.

questions.explanation: A dispositional attribution is an explanation of behavior that points to the person's own traits or character.

questions.stem: In the 1940s, surgeons cut the connections to patients' frontal lobes to calm them, often leaving them permanently listless. Which procedure was this?

options.why: Electroconvulsive therapy is the treatment for severe depression in which a brief electric current is passed through the brain of an anesthetized patient.
Transcranial magnetic stimulation is the treatment in which repeated magnetic pulses are applied to the surface of the brain to treat depression.
Psychotropic medication is any drug that acts on the brain to treat the symptoms of a psychological disorder.
Correct. A lobotomy is the now-abandoned form of psychosurgery that cut the nerves connecting the frontal lobes to the rest of the brain.

questions.explanation: A lobotomy is the now-abandoned form of psychosurgery that cut the nerves connecting the frontal lobes to the rest of the brain.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes NREM stage 3?

options.text: The sleep stage with rapid eye movements, vivid dreams, an active brain and relaxed muscles
options.why: That describes REM sleep.

options.text: The deep sleep stage marked by slow delta waves, in which a person is hard to wake
options.why: Correct. This is what NREM stage 3 means.

options.text: The brief, light first stage of sleep, in which a person may have hypnagogic sensations such as falling
options.why: That describes NREM stage 1.

options.text: The tendency to have more REM sleep after being deprived of it
options.why: That describes REM rebound.

questions.explanation: NREM stage 3 is the deep sleep stage marked by slow delta waves, in which a person is hard to wake.

questions.stem: Which of the following would be a confounding variable in this study?

options.text: Each one was assigned to a condition at random
options.why: Random assignment reduces confounding; it is not a confound.

options.text: One group differed from the other in the color of the drinks

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as in classical conditioning, the originally neutral stimulus that triggers a response after being paired with another stimulus?

options.why: The unconditioned stimulus is in classical conditioning, the stimulus that triggers a response naturally, without learning.
The unconditioned response is in classical conditioning, the natural, unlearned response to a stimulus.
Correct. The conditioned stimulus is in classical conditioning, the originally neutral stimulus that triggers a response after being paired with another stimulus.
The conditioned response is in classical conditioning, the learned response to a previously neutral stimulus.

questions.explanation: The conditioned stimulus is in classical conditioning, the originally neutral stimulus that triggers a response after being paired with another stimulus.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes gross motor skills?

options.text: A harmful agent, such as alcohol or a virus, that can damage an embryo or fetus
options.why: That describes a teratogen.

options.text: The process by which some animals form a strong attachment to the first moving object they see
options.why: That describes imprinting.

options.text: The movements that use large muscles, such as crawling, walking and jumping
options.why: Correct. This is what gross motor skills means.

options.text: A limited time early in life when certain experiences must occur for normal development
options.why: That describes a critical period.

questions.explanation: Gross motor skills is the movements that use large muscles, such as crawling, walking and jumping.

questions.stem: A baby whose cries are answered with food and comfort learns that the world is dependable. Which of Erikson's stages is this?

options.why: Correct. Trust versus mistrust is Erikson's stage in infancy, in which babies learn whether their needs will be met.
Industry versus inferiority is Erikson's stage in elementary school, in which children learn to feel competent or else feel inadequate.
Autonomy versus shame and doubt is Erikson's stage in toddlerhood, in which children learn to do things for themselves.
Initiative versus guilt is Erikson's stage in the preschool years, in which children learn to start tasks and carry out plans.

questions.explanation: Trust versus mistrust is Erikson's stage in infancy, in which babies learn whether their needs will be met.

questions.stem: After the study, the researchers explained its full purpose to every participant and answered their questions. What is this called?

Replication is repeating a study.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the schedule in which the behavior is reinforced every time it occurs?

options.why: A variable-ratio schedule is the schedule in which the behavior is reinforced after an unpredictable number of responses.
Correct. Continuous reinforcement is the schedule in which the behavior is reinforced every time it occurs.
A fixed-interval schedule is the schedule in which the first response after a set amount of time is reinforced.
A fixed-ratio schedule is the schedule in which the behavior is reinforced after a set number of responses.

questions.explanation: Continuous reinforcement is the schedule in which the behavior is reinforced every time it occurs.

questions.stem: In a group project with one shared grade, each of the five members does less work than they would on an individual project. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Social facilitation is the improved performance on simple or well-learned tasks in the presence of others.
Deindividuation is the loss of self-awareness and self-restraint in group situations that provide arousal and anonymity.
Diffusion of responsibility is the reduced sense of personal duty to act when other people are present.
Correct. Social loafing is the tendency for people to put in less effort when working in a group than when working alone.

questions.explanation: Social loafing is the tendency for people to put in less effort when working in a group than when working alone.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes phantom limb sensation?

options.text: The sense of balance and head position, based on the semicircular canals of the inner ear

options.text: The feeling of pain or touch in a limb that has been amputated

options.why: That describes kinesthesis.

options.why: That describes the gate control theory.

questions.explanation: Phantom limb sensation is the feeling of pain or touch in a limb that has been amputated.

questions.stem: Yuki reads a note with several letters smudged, yet she understands every word because she knows what the sentence should say. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Inattentional blindness is the failure to notice a visible object because attention is directed elsewhere.

The cocktail party effect is the ability to notice personally important information, such as your name, in an unattended conversation.
A perceptual set is a readiness to perceive something in a particular way because of expectations.

questions.explanation: Top-down processing is perception that is guided by experience, expectations and context.

questions.stem: To treat a child's fear of rabbits, a therapist gives the child a favorite snack while a rabbit is slowly brought closer. Which technique is this?

options.why: Correct. Counterconditioning is the replacing of an unwanted response to a stimulus with a new response, by pairing the stimulus with something pleasant.
Habituation is the decrease in response to a stimulus that is presented over and over.
One-trial conditioning is learning that happens after a single pairing of two stimuli.
A taste aversion is a learned dislike of a food that was followed by illness.

questions.explanation: Counterconditioning is the replacing of an unwanted response to a stimulus with a new response, by pairing the stimulus with something pleasant.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the positive psychological change that some people experience after struggling with a very difficult event?

options.why: Correct. Posttraumatic growth is the positive psychological change that some people experience after struggling with a very difficult event.
Subjective well-being is a person's own evaluation of how happy and satisfied they are with life.
Resilience is the ability to recover and adapt well after stress or hardship.
Signature strengths is the positive character traits, such as kindness or curiosity, that are most central to a particular person.

questions.explanation: Posttraumatic growth is the positive psychological change that some people experience after struggling with a very difficult event.

questions.stem: Some cells in the brain do not send impulses themselves; they supply nutrients to neurons and clean up waste. Which cells are these?

options.why: The reflex arc is the simple automatic pathway in which the spinal cord produces a response before the brain is aware of the stimulus.
Correct. Glial cells is the cells that support, nourish, insulate and protect neurons.
Interneurons is the neurons inside the brain and spinal cord that pass messages between sensory inputs and motor outputs.

questions.explanation: Glial cells is the cells that support, nourish, insulate and protect neurons.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes insomnia?

options.text: Sleepwalking, which occurs during deep NREM sleep
options.why: That describes somnambulism.

options.text: A sleep disorder with sudden, uncontrollable attacks of sleep, often straight into REM sleep
options.why: That describes narcolepsy.

options.text: A sleep disorder with ongoing difficulty falling asleep or staying asleep

options.why: That describes REM sleep behavior disorder.

questions.explanation: Insomnia is a sleep disorder with ongoing difficulty falling asleep or staying asleep.

questions.stem: Why did the researchers assign the participants to the two conditions at random?

options.text: So that the two groups would be similar at the start, and any difference could be attributed to the independent variable

questions.stem: For three years, Otto has felt low and tired on most days, though he still manages to work. Which disorder does this suggest?

options.why: Bipolar I disorder is the disorder in which a person has full manic episodes, usually alternating with depression.
Mania is a state of extreme energy, overconfidence, racing thoughts and little need for sleep.
Correct. Persistent depressive disorder is the disorder in which a person has a mildly depressed mood on most days for at least two years.
Bipolar II disorder is the disorder in which a person alternates between depression and a milder form of mania called hypomania.

questions.explanation: Persistent depressive disorder is the disorder in which a person has a mildly depressed mood on most days for at least two years.

questions.stem: After a message has been sent, the sending neuron takes back the neurotransmitter molecules that remain in the gap. What is this process called?

Correct. Reuptake is the process in which the sending neuron reabsorbs leftover neurotransmitters from the synapse.
Depolarization is the change in which positive ions rush into the axon and make the inside less negative.
The action potential is the brief electrical charge that travels down the axon when a neuron fires.

questions.explanation: Reuptake is the process in which the sending neuron reabsorbs leftover neurotransmitters from the synapse.

questions.stem: Without evidence, Hugo is convinced that his coworkers, neighbors and friends are all plotting against him, and he has felt this way for years. Which disorder does this suggest?

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the first phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the sympathetic nervous system is suddenly activated?

The general adaptation syndrome is Selye's three-phase description of the body's response to long-term stress: alarm, resistance and exhaustion.

questions.stem: Students who quiz themselves on a chapter remember more a week later than students who read the chapter twice. This best illustrates which of the following?

questions.stem: A whisper and a shout at the same pitch differ in loudness. Which property of the sound waves differs?

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the monocular depth cue in which surfaces look smoother and less detailed as they get farther away?

questions.title: Article analysis: a study of stress

parts.prompt: Identify the research method used in the study.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the method as an experiment.
rubric.example: The study is an experiment: the researchers manipulated a variable and randomly assigned the subjects to conditions.

parts.prompt: State the operational definition of stress.

rubric.criterion: States how the variable was measured in this study.
rubric.example: Stress was defined as the level of the stress hormone cortisol in a saliva sample from each participant.

parts.prompt: Describe the meaning of the difference between the two group averages.

rubric.criterion: Accurately describes which group scored higher or lower and what that means for the variable measured.
rubric.example: The meditation group had lower cortisol levels. On average, the value was 9.8 for the group that meditated and 13.5 for the group that listened to an audiobook, and a p value of 0.01 means a difference this large is unlikely to be due to chance.

parts.prompt: Identify at least one ethical guideline applied by the researchers.

rubric.criterion: Identifies an ethical guideline that the summary shows was followed.
rubric.example: Informed consent: participants agreed to take part after being told about the study. (Also acceptable: debriefing; the right to withdraw; approval by an institutional review board.)

parts.prompt: Explain the extent to which the research findings may or may not be generalizable, using specific and relevant evidence from the study.

rubric.criterion: Explains a limit (or strength) of generalizability with reference to the sample.
rubric.example: The sample was 84 office workers from one city, so the findings may not apply to people of other ages, cultures or backgrounds. Because the sample was not randomly selected from a wider population, it may not be representative.

parts.prompt: Explain how at least one of the research findings supports or refutes the researchers' hypothesis.

rubric.criterion: Uses a specific finding from the study as evidence.
rubric.example: The meditation group had lower cortisol levels. (9.8 compared with 13.5).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the finding supports the hypothesis, using a psychological concept.
rubric.example: This supports the hypothesis that the daily activity affects stress. Because subjects were randomly assigned, the difference can be attributed to the daily activity. The finding illustrates emotion-focused coping: managing the emotional and physical reaction to stress lowers the body's stress response.

questions.title: Evidence-based question: Do rewards increase motivation?

parts.prompt: Propose a specific and defensible claim, based in psychological science, that responds to the question.

rubric.criterion: States a claim that answers the question and can be supported by the sources.
rubric.example: Rewards increase a behavior while they last, but they can reduce intrinsic motivation, so the behavior falls when the rewards stop.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using at least one piece of specific and relevant evidence from one of the sources. (ii) Explain how the evidence supports your claim, using a psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding learned in AP Psychology.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from one source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source A, children promised a certificate later chose to draw for 6.5 minutes, compared with 13.8 minutes for children who were not rewarded.

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim through intrinsic and extrinsic motivation: the reward gave the children an external reason for drawing, which weakened their desire to draw for its own sake.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a psychological concept in the explanation.
rubric.example: The concept must be named and applied correctly, as in the model explanation.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using an additional piece of specific and relevant evidence from a different source. (ii) Explain how this evidence supports your claim, using a different psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from a different source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source B, workers paid a bonus made more sales (41 compared with 33), but their sales fell to 30 when the bonus ended.

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim through operant conditioning: the bonus acted as positive reinforcement, which increased the behavior, and when reinforcement stopped the behavior declined (extinction).

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a different psychological concept from the one used in part B.
rubric.example: The concept must differ from the one used in part B and be applied correctly.
